facts.text: TprTrigger is an ophyd BaseInterface/Device for an individual TPR trigger
The TprTrigger channel argument is an integer from 0 through 11
TimingMode has the members LCLS1 = 1 and LCLS2 = 2
TprTrigger formats the channel as :CHnn_ and the trigger as :TRGnn_ and rejects any other timing mode
enable_ch_cmd and enable_trg_cmd are EpicsSignal channel-enable and trigger-enable commands
enable() calls enable_ch() then enable_trg(); disable() calls disable_ch() then disable_trg()
enable_ch and enable_trg put 1; disable_ch and disable_trg put 0
ns_delay is a MultiDerivedSignal over delay_ticks, delay_taps and delay_setpoint with the doc 'Get/set trigger delay in ns'
width is a MultiDerivedSignal over width_ticks and width_setpoint with the doc 'Get/set trigger width in nsec'
TPR_TICK_NS is 70 / 13, from the 1.3 GHz phase-reference line divided by 7, and TPR_TAP_NS is 0.08
The delay read is delay_ticks times TPR_TICK_NS plus delay_taps times TPR_TAP_NS, and the width read is width_ticks times TPR_TICK_NS
_put_last writes the value only to the last signal of a MultiDerivedSignal
delay_setpoint is the TDES EpicsSignal and width_setpoint the TWID EpicsSignal of the trigger
AggregateSignal.get calls get on every member signal and recalculates the value
MultiDerivedSignal.put calls set, and set passes the calculate_on_put mapping to utils.set_many
set_many logs an exception raised by a member set, re-raises it only with raise_on_set_failure, and returns a finished Status when no member set started
eventrate is an EpicsSignalRO for the channel event rates
label is an EpicsSignal for the channel description

operator_required.name: delay_ns
operator_required.reason: no line of the clone states a trigger-delay range: ns_delay is derived from delay_ticks and delay_taps (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:95-101) and neither the ticks/taps PV limits nor a delay range is written in the clone; the site supplies the allowed delay range in ns

operator_required.name: width_ns
operator_required.reason: no line of the clone states a trigger-width range: width is derived from width_ticks and width_setpoint (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:117-123) and neither PV limit nor a width range is written in the clone; the site supplies the allowed width range in ns

safe_state.description: trigger channel and trigger output disabled: disable_ch and disable_trg put 0 to the enable commands, and both read back 0 before the stop is reported; the readback is the IOC's enable records, not a measured absence of pulses, and equipment fired by other channels is not stopped
